title: Window and Door Rebates in Victoria 2026: $100 Each, Up to $2,000
desc: BC Hydro pays $100 per window or door in Victoria for U-factor 1.22 or lower. 31,310 households live in pre-1981 homes, but only 4,515 own an older house. Rules and steps.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Victoria
lead: Victoria has the oldest homes of any BC city we cover and some of the mildest winters. Replacing old windows here is as much about comfort, noise and condensation as the heating bill.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for windows and doors in Victoria
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's window and door page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity. FortisBC lists the same $100 per opening for its gas customers.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: Paid for each window or door that replaces an existing one between a heated space and outdoors.

cards.title: Cap
cards.note: That is 20 openings at $100 each. A bay window counts as one opening.

cards.title: Energy rating
cards.note: The window or door must have a maximum U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K, which is BC Hydro's Tier 2 level.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro adds a bonus when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can apply for free upgrades.

after_cards:
A Victoria character house

An older two-storey with 15 windows and one back door is 16 openings. At $100 each that is $1,600. A bay window counts as one opening even when it has several panes, so a bay front is cheaper for the rebate than listing each pane. These sums come from the posted rule.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 49,220 households in Victoria. Of those, 31,310 (64%) live in homes built before 1981, the highest share in our BC list. But 70% of households are in apartments and 60% rent, so only 4,515 are owner-occupied detached houses from before 1981. For that smaller group, old windows may be the biggest comfort gain available.

Victoria's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 3.0°C and the coldest day was -10.6°C. Heating bills are lower than in the Interior, so the savings from windows alone are modest. Many people replace windows here for noise, condensation and draft control, with the rebate covering part of the cost.

The rebate counts rough openings, not panes. Each rough opening where a window or door was replaced is one opening. A bay window made of several sections is one opening. Skylights are not eligible. Windows and doors must replace existing units in the building envelope, between a heated space and an unheated space like the outdoors.

All upgrades must be installed by a licensed contractor with a GST number and a valid BC business licence for the trade. Self-installation is not eligible. The windows and doors must be new, in good working order, and not previously installed in another home. Rebates also cannot exceed the cost on the invoice, so ask each bidder to price the units and the install separately.

If your old windows are wood frames you want to keep, repair or add storm panels may be worth pricing. Those do not earn a rebate, but they can cost less.

Condo and apartment buildings are not eligible for this program, and BC Hydro runs a separate program for them. In a rental house the BC Hydro account holder applies, and anyone else needs the account holder's signed consent form. Townhomes qualify only when each unit has its own meter and the account is not in a strata corporation's name.

BC Hydro sends income-qualified customers to the CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program instead, and the two cannot be combined. The 2026 program document lists no insulation or window rebates, so the free Energy Conservation Assistance Program is the route to ask about.
claim_steps: Confirm that your heat is mainly electric and the home is at least 12 months old.
Get quotes that list each window or door with its U-factor.
Keep the invoice and photos of the manufacturer label on each unit.
Add insulation or a water heater to the same application to check the bonus.
faq: How many windows can I claim?
Up to 20 openings at $100 each, for a $2,000 maximum. Count rough openings, not panes.
Does a bay window count as more than one?
No. A bay window is one rough opening.
No. BC Hydro's page says skylights are not eligible.
Can I install the windows myself?
No. Self-installation is not eligible. A licensed contractor with a GST number and a BC business licence must install them.
Yes. It must be 1.22 W/m2-K or lower.
